rationale: Use own colour and coordinates modulo 3. Zeros at residues (0,1), (0,2), (1,1), and (2,1) become 4, 5, 6, and 3 respectively; other residues stay zero. Demonstration 5 shows these changes at (0,1), (0,2), (4,1), and (3,1). Nonzero colours remain unchanged.

Use own colour and row/column parity. Zero becomes 3 at even-row odd-column positions, 4 at odd-row even-column positions, and 2 at odd-row odd-column positions. Colour 2 becomes 7 at even/even positions, as demonstration 7 shows at (2,2), (2,4), and (2,6).

Use own colour and border status. Interior colours 1, 2, and 3 become 4, 5, and 9; border colour 3 becomes 0. Demonstration 2 has interior 3 at (2,2) becoming 9 and border 3 at (0,2) becoming 0. Zeros and border colours 1 and 2 retain their colours.

Use own colour plus both nonzero row and column sets. In demonstration 6, zeros in column 2 become 4 where the row set is {1,2,3} and the column set is {2}. In demonstration 4, zeros in rows with set {1,2} and columns with set {2} become 5; demonstration 1 also shows 5 for row set {1,2} and column set {3}.

Use own colour and the nonzero row set. Rows containing {2,3} recolour zeros to 4; rows containing {1,2} recolour 1 to 8; rows containing {1,2,3} recolour zeros to 7 and 2 to 6. Demonstration 1 exhibits the first two cases, and demonstration 3 exhibits the third.

Use own colour and both nonzero row and column sets. Colour 3 becomes 2 when both sets are {1,2,3}, as at (3,4) in demonstration 1. With row set {1,3} and column set {2,3}, 3 becomes 5 and zero becomes 6, shown in demonstration 9 at (3,3) and (1,3). Colour 2 becomes 4 with row set {1,2,3} and column set {1,2}, shown at (4,6) in demonstration 4.

Use own colour and border status. Border zeros become 4 and interior zeros become 5; interior 2 becomes 0, and border 3 becomes 9. Demonstration 1 shows each case at (0,1), (1,1), (2,3), and (0,0). Other colour/status combinations retain their colours.

Use own colour and the nonzero row set. Zeros become 1 for sets {1} or {2,3}, 2 for {1,3}, and 3 for {3}. Demonstration 2 shows {3}, {1}, and {1,3}; demonstration 6 shows {2,3}. Other row sets and all nonzero pixels stay unchanged.

Use own colour and border status. Border zeros become 2, interior zeros become 3, border 1 becomes 0, and border 2 becomes 4. Demonstration 1 shows these at (0,0), (1,2), (0,1), and (0,6); interior nonzero pixels and all colour 3 pixels remain unchanged.

Use the full 3x3 neighbourhood, including out-of-grid markers. Demonstration 5 changes the top-left zero to 2 where its right, lower, and lower-right neighbours are all zero. All other demonstrated neighbourhoods preserve the centre colour; unseen neighbourhoods also preserve it.
